To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
teachers are implementing Continuous Assessment in their classrooms, but they do not have sufficient knowledge and skills to do this in an effective manner.

the implementation of the CA programme was not successful because teachers did not understand the purpose of the assessment and the content of the curriculum, and they were unable to use their knowledge of the subject matter to make appropriate choices.
teachers’ implementation of CA was constrained by their limited curriculum literacy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What are the challenges that teachers experience in implementing CA as a tool for curriculum improvement?
the nature of teachers’ curriculum literacy and how it affects their ability to use CA effectively in the classroom.
the ways in which teachers’ curriculum knowledge and practice are shaped by the demands of CA, and the extent to which they are able to meet those demands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CA is an assessment tool which is used by the teachers in their classrooms to measure the learners’ performance in terms of their understanding of the lesson objectives, and to determine whether they are ready to move on to the next lesson.
the teachers’ curriculum literacy is still in its infancy and that the teachers need further training in the use of CA.
the teachers in the sample were not able to use CA in ways that would promote the development of their students’ literacy skills.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
teachers need to be supported in their understanding of the curriculum they teach and the ways in which they can use CA to improve the learning of their pupils.
teachers are able to use CA to meet the requirements for lesson objectives but that this does not necessarily translate into improved learning for their students.

the teachers’ curriculum literacy is not only about the content and the pedagogies that are used to teach the content, but also about how the teachers make sense of the curriculum as a whole and how it is implemented in the classroom.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers’ understanding of the curriculum is a critical factor that influences their ability to use CA effectively.
the CA programme is an opportunity to develop teachers’ curriculum literacy and to improve the quality of teaching and learning in Swaziland.
teachers are not passive agents in the implementation of curriculum reforms.
